contents.name: §5.4.2 eqs. (5.30)-(5.32): four-force law dP^μ/dτ=qF^{μν}U_ν and its coordinate reduction dp/dt=q(E+u×B)

contents.name: §5.5.1 eqs. (5.34)-(5.35): nonrelativistic particle action and the derivation of m ẍ=q(E+ẋ×B) with the boundary term discarded
contents.reason: The nonrelativistic action and its Euler-Lagrange reduction belong to the nonrelativistic mechanics track's stationary-action page; this pair builds only the relativistic fixed-endpoint statement and does not claim the Galilean branch.

contents.name: §5.5.2 eqs. (5.36)-(5.37): relativistic particle action −mc²∫√(1−ẋ²/c²)dt and the coupling −qφ+qẋ·A
contents.support: The prescribed-field particle action and its coupling; the pair states the covariant fixed-endpoint functional over future timelike C² worldlines and rederives the equation of motion in its own conventions.

contents.name: §5.5.2 'The Covariant Action' eqs. (5.38)-(5.40): manifestly Lorentz-invariant action −mc∫dσ√(η_{μν}Ẋ^μẊ^ν), proper-time relation, reparametrisation invariance and the mass-shell constraint P^μP_μ=m²c²
contents.reason: Reparametrisation-invariant covariant particle actions, the mass-shell constraint and the constraint analysis belong to relativistic particle mechanics; the fixed-endpoint functional used here is the free-parameter one and this pair makes no reparametrisation or constraint claim.

contents.name: §5.5.2 eq. (5.41): covariant coupling q∫A_μ(X)dX^μ
contents.support: The covariant coupling term of the particle functional; the pair uses exactly this term with a prescribed C² external potential.

contents.name: §5.5.1 remark: no Lagrangian formulation of electromagnetism involves only E and B; the potentials are obligatory
contents.support: The definition takes the potential A_μ on a neighbourhood of the region as its object; the remark records why the functional is defined on potentials rather than on E,B.

contents.name: §5.5.3 eq. (5.42): Maxwell action −(1/4μ0c)∫d⁴x F_{μν}F^{μν}, its Lorentz invariance and the expansion to ∫dtd³x(ε0E²/2−B²/(2μ0))
contents.support: The field functional; the pair instantiates it with the (-,+,+,+) conventions of def-em-electromagnetic-tensor, the source coupling +j^νA_ν and the explicit c⁻¹ normalization fixed by the definition contract.

contents.name: §5.5.3 variation display of eq. (5.42) and the sourced eq. (5.43): δS=(1/(μ0c))∫(∂_μF^{μν})δA_ν after discarding the total derivative, ∂_μF^{μν}=μ0J^μ, and 'only half the Maxwell equations' from the variation
contents.support: The expansion-antisymmetry-integration-by-parts route and the coefficient equation; the pair makes the discarded total derivative explicit through the compact-support hypothesis of lem-em-compact-field-variation and rederives all signs in its own dictionary.

contents.name: §5.5.3 gauge-shift paragraph: S→S+(1/c)∫(∂_μχ)J^μ=S−(1/c)∫χ∂_μJ^μ, invariant iff ∂_μJ^μ=0
contents.support: The exact gauge difference and the equivalence between compact gauge invariance and source conservation; the pair states both directions with the fundamental lemma and the distributional reading.

contents.name: §5.5.3 combined particle-plus-field action and the point-particle current J^μ=qc∫dσ(dX^μ/dσ)δ⁴(x−X(σ))
contents.reason: The combined action varies the electromagnetic field and charged worldlines with the particles’ own singular field; it is excluded by the approved smooth prescribed-current field sector and the separate prescribed-external-potential particle sector. A fixed-endpoint charge variation in an external field does not establish this coupled singular system, and no current or future owning-page completion is claimed.

contents.name: §5.5.3 'Theta Term' paragraphs: F̃^{μν}F_{μν} as a total derivative and its quantum role
contents.reason: Topological theta-term and quantum-symmetry content lies outside classical electromagnetism and has no consumer in this run's classical scope.

contents.name: Box 1: functionals, extremisation and the Euler-Lagrange equations
contents.reason: The general one-variable functional and Euler-Lagrange framework belongs to the nonrelativistic mechanics track; this pair consumes only the concrete finite-region functionals and their recorded variation lemmas.

contents.name: §3.1 eqs. (3.2)-(3.6): S=∫dτ(−m₀c²+qẋ·A) for a particle in a given field, fixed endpoints, elimination of τ, and the derivation of the equation of motion
contents.support: The fixed-endpoint action over a worldline in a given field and the resulting equation of motion; the pair states the same computation in the framework's C² future timelike class and its index conventions.

contents.name: §3.1 eqs. (3.7)-(3.8): nonrelativistic reduction L=½m₀ẋ²−qφ
contents.reason: The Galilean reduction of the charged-particle action is owned by the nonrelativistic mechanics track and is not claimed by this pair.

contents.name: §3.2 eqs. (3.10)-(3.16): Lagrangian field theory on spacetime, S=∫d⁴x L(φ,∂φ), variations vanishing on the boundary
contents.support: The finite-region field-functional scheme with compactly supported smooth variations; the pair's definition and its cited compact-variation lemma instantiate exactly this scheme for the electromagnetic potential.

contents.name: §3.3-§3.5: real scalar field, Klein-Gordon and Dirac equations
contents.reason: Non-electromagnetic field Lagrangians and spinor fields have no consumer among this run's classical-electromagnetism pages.

contents.name: §3.6 eqs. (3.29)-(3.32): L_vac=−¼F·F, the expansion −½(E²/c²−B²), and the variation giving half of Maxwell's equations
contents.support: The quadratic vacuum Lagrangian and the variation-produced field equations, with the same structural split: the dynamical equations come from the variation, the remaining Maxwell equations from F being a curl.

contents.name: §3.6 eqs. (3.33)-(3.36): interaction term j·A, the swarm current, the sourced action and the sourced field equations
contents.support: The source coupling of the functional and the identification of the current that multiplies the potential; the pair uses the smooth source fields j=(cρ,J) of def-em-sources.

contents.name: §3.6 closing remark: the other four Maxwell equations do not come from minimising the action but from F being the 4-curl of A
contents.support: The theorem's homogeneous clause is exactly this structural remark: the cyclic identity holds because F=dA with smooth A and mixed partials commute.

contents.name: §3.7 eqs. (3.37)-(3.39): internal-symmetry Noether current and 'e.m. charge conservation', including the observation that an arbitrary gauge direction at a point forces ∂_μF^{μν}=0
contents.support: The theorem's converse direction absorbs the source's observation that the gauge direction can be chosen arbitrarily; the pair replaces the source's informal 'any vector at a given point' step with the componentwise fundamental lemma and does not adopt the general Noether formalism.

contents.name: §3.7 eqs. (3.40)-(3.45): Klein-Gordon current and particle-flux conservation
contents.reason: Quantum-field particle currents have no consumer in this classical-electromagnetism pair.

contents.name: §3.8 eqs. (3.46)-(3.53): Noether energy-momentum tensor, its symmetrisation, and the remark that a fixed j·A breaks translation invariance
contents.reason: This pair builds no Noether theorem and no stress-energy derivation; the framework's covariant stress-energy is supplied by em-lorentz-covariant-formulation, and the remark is scope context only.

contents.name: §16 eqs. (16.1), (16.4): particle action −mc∫ds−(e/c)∫A_idx^i and Lagrangian L=−mc²√(1−v²/c²)+(e/c)A·v−eφ

contents.name: §27 eqs. (27.1)-(27.3): additive decomposition S=S_f+S_m+S_{mf} of the total action
contents.support: The separation of the field functional from the matter and interaction parts; the pair defines the field functional with the interaction density j^νA_ν and keeps matter dynamics outside its scope.

contents.name: §27 eqs. (27.4)-(27.6): S_f=−(1/16π)∫F_{ik}F^{ik}dΩ=(1/8π)∫(E²−H²)dVdt and the field Lagrangian
contents.support: The quadratic field functional whose SI form the pair fixes as c⁻¹∫(−F²/(4μ0)+j^νA_ν)dλ; only the structure is reused, with every constant and sign rederived.

contents.name: §27 eq. (27.7): total action of field plus particles
contents.reason: The combined action varies the electromagnetic field and charged worldlines with the particles’ own singular field; it is excluded by the approved smooth prescribed-current field sector and the separate prescribed-external-potential particle sector. A fixed-endpoint charge variation in an external field does not establish this coupled singular system, and no current or future owning-page completion is claimed.

contents.name: §27 sign discussion: (∂A/∂t)² must appear with positive sign, 'a must be negative', and the resulting minimum language for S_f
contents.support: The source ties the sign of the quadratic field term to a minimum requirement; the example's exact computation shows that with the adopted sign the stationary point of the source-free functional is a saddle, so the 'minimum' wording is not adopted while no claim of the source is contradicted.

contents.name: §28: four-dimensional current vector and the δ-function charge density
contents.support: The four-current structure of the source term; the pair identifies j=(cρ,J) through def-em-sources and explicitly excludes the singular δ-function branch from its source class.

contents.name: §29 eqs. (29.1)-(29.4): integral and differential equation of continuity and its four-dimensional form
contents.support: The continuity equation that the gauge theorem links to compact gauge invariance; the pair routes the smooth branch through pthm-em-charge-continuity and the chart identity ∂_μj^μ=∂_tρ+div J.

contents.name: §30 eq. (30.1): variation of the action with fixed current, interchange of indices, integration by parts and discarding of the boundary term, yielding the second pair of Maxwell equations
contents.support: The variation computation producing the inhomogeneous field equations; the pair makes the boundary term explicitly vanish through compact support and derives the same coefficient equation in its own conventions.

contents.name: §23-§25: the electromagnetic field tensor, Lorentz transformation of the field and invariants
contents.reason: The tensor dictionary and transformation content is owned by the covariant-formulation page, which is this page's declared prerequisite; this pair consumes those interfaces as context only.

contents.name: §31-§33: field energy density, energy flux and the energy-momentum tensor
contents.reason: Field energy and stress-energy are owned by em-energy-momentum-and-angular-balance and em-lorentz-covariant-formulation; no item of this pair consumes them.

note: Convention dictionary. The three treatments use other signatures and normalizations: Tong and Binney work with a (+,-,-,-) metric and Binney normalizes the vacuum Lagrangian as −¼F·F with the coupling j·A inside a minus sign; Landau-Lifshitz use Gaussian units with S_f=−(1/16π)∫F_{ik}F^{ik}dΩ and the particle coupling −(e/c)∫A_idx^i. This pair uses the (-,+,+,+) form η of def-em-electromagnetic-tensor, the potential/current dictionary F_{0i}=−E_i/c, F_{ij}=ε_{ijk}B_k, j=(cρ,J), the density −F_{μν}F^{μν}/(4μ0)+j^νA_ν and the conclusion ∂_μF^{μν}=−μ0j^ν. Every sign and constant is rederived in the pair's conventions; only the structure of the variation, the gauge shift and the fixed-endpoint curve computation is reused. The Binney rows were read in the repository's OCR text of the same PDF because the PDF's embedded fonts defeat direct text extraction; the fetch stamp below is on the PDF itself.
